title: TaxonomyNode (and shared vocabulary definitions)
description: A single node of the visual taxonomy. This file is ALSO the shared vocabulary module for the whole project: the canonical VISUAL_CATEGORY / INTENT_CATEGORY enums, the taxonomy id grammar, id prefixes, license ids, formatter modes, prompt slots, the category-arity table and the category->prompt-slot table live here in $defs and are $ref'd by every other schema. This file intentionally has NO external $ref so it can always be resolved first. Taxonomy nodes power the AI-free product: aliases[] + related[] form the inverted index behind keyword search, prompt_fragment/model_hints are what the formatter emits, conflicts_with[] + exclusivity_group drive conflict detection.

id.description: Stable, globally unique, exactly two dotted segments: '<category>.<slug>'. Hierarchy is NEVER encoded in the id (use parent), so re-parenting a node never breaks stored intents, mixes or recipes.

category.description: MUST equal the namespace segment of id.

label.description: Human-readable display text for chips and browse tiles. For lens nodes the label carries the hedge, e.g. id 'lens.35mm_like' -> label '35mm-like perspective'.

aliases.description: Alternate spellings, colloquialisms, jargon and misspellings a user might type. Primary fuel for AI-free keyword search. e.g. camera_angle.low_angle -> ['low angle','worm eye','from below','looking up','hero shot'].

related.description: Adjacent-but-different nodes. Used for one-hop query expansion in AI-free search and for 'you might also mean' suggestions. NOT a hierarchy edge and NOT a conflict edge.

parent.description: Parent node id, or null for a category root. MUST be in the same category. Cycles are forbidden.

children.description: Derived cache of child ids; parent is authoritative. Loaders MUST be able to rebuild children from parent.

description.description: Plain-language explanation shown in the browse modal so a user who does not know the term can still choose it visually.

examples.description: Short illustrative phrases, e.g. 'shot from knee height looking up at the subject'.

visual_hint.description: Reference id whose thumbnail represents this node in the visual browse grid, or null. Serves the 'I don't know what Low Angle means, let me choose it visually' use case.

visual_hint_pool.description: Optional extra reference ids for a multi-thumbnail browse tile.

conflicts_with.description: Explicit pairwise incompatibility, usable ACROSS categories (e.g. clothing.dress conflicts_with clothing.trousers). Conflict detection is the union of: category arity rule, shared exclusivity_group, and this list. SHOULD be declared symmetrically; loaders MUST treat it as symmetric regardless.

exclusivity_group.description: Conflict bucket. Two chips in the same category sharing a non-null exclusivity_group conflict. In a single_dominant category, a node with exclusivity_group=null is a MODIFIER and never conflicts (e.g. camera_angle.dutch_tilt, pose.arms_crossed, weather.fog). Reserved values: garment_top, garment_bottom, garment_outer, garment_full_body, footwear, headwear, locomotion, speed, key_level, light_direction, frame_geometry, interiority, location, camera_move_primary, pose_base, time_of_day, weather_primary, palette_scheme, era.

media_scope.description: Which reference media types may legitimately carry this node. camera_motion nodes are video-only.

still_inferable.description: Only meaningful for category 'motion'. True when a single still frame can legitimately evidence this node (motion.hair_movement, motion.clothing_movement, motion.jumping mid-air). Gates INV-VID-3: an analyzer_image chip in 'motion' is only valid for a still_inferable node and is capped at confidence 0.6.

prompt_fragment.description: The exact text the generic formatter emits for this node. Defaults to label when absent. Lens fragments MUST be hedged (see the lens if/then below).

negative_fragment.description: Text emitted into the StructuredPrompt 'constraints' slot when a chip carrying this node has negate=true. Falls back to 'no <prompt_fragment>'.

model_hints.description: Per-formatter-mode override of prompt_fragment. Unknown or missing modes MUST fall back to prompt_fragment, then to label. Model backends are never hardcoded: a new mode is a new key here, no code change.

search_boost.description: Multiplier applied to the AI-free keyword scorer for this node.

sort_order.description: Display order within the parent group; ties broken by label.

i18n.description: Localized label/aliases/description. Localized aliases are indexed by keyword search alongside the base aliases. prompt_fragment is NEVER localized.

deprecated.description: True when the node must no longer be offered in browse or search results. Existing stored chips remain valid and are displayed with a deprecation marker.

replaced_by.description: Successor node id. REQUIRED (non-null) when deprecated is true and a successor exists; normalizeVisualIntent rewrites deprecated values to replaced_by and records the rewrite.

x_ext.description: Vendor/experimental extension bucket. Never read by core code.

allOf.$comment: INV-TAX-3 / lens honesty rule. A lens node that names a focal length must use the _like suffix, and every lens fragment must be hedged so the product never asserts EXIF it cannot know.
INV-VID-2 support: camera_motion is a temporal property; only video can evidence it.
still_inferable is only meaningful inside category 'motion'.
A deprecated node must say so explicitly; replaced_by may be null only when no successor exists.

schema_version.description: MAJOR.MINOR schema version of the persisted object. MAJOR bump = breaking (field removed/renamed/retyped, enum value removed, semantics changed). MINOR bump = additive only. Readers MUST accept any MINOR within the same MAJOR and MUST ignore unknown properties introduced by a higher MINOR; readers MUST refuse or migrate a different MAJOR.

id_slug.description: Slug body used after every id prefix. Minted ids are ALWAYS lowercase (slugify + hash); mixed case is accepted only so hand-authored fixtures and the brief's own shorthand (img_A) stay valid. Ids are compared case-SENSITIVELY: never mint two ids differing only in case.

visual_category.$comment: THE canonical category key set. 20 members, brief order. Referenced by VisualIntent, Reference.visual_attributes, ReferenceMix.use, StructuredPrompt mapping and conflict detection.

intent_category.$comment: VISUAL_CATEGORY minus 'props'. These 19 are exactly the array-valued keys of VisualIntent, which the brief fixes at 20 keys (19 arrays + confidence). 'props' remains a first-class taxonomy/reference/mix category and is carried into VisualIntent as a 'scene' chip with origin_category='props'.

taxonomy_id.description: '<visual_category>.<snake_case_slug>'. Exactly two segments. Examples: framing.medium_shot, lens.35mm_like, camera_motion.dolly_in, clothing.oversized_hoodie.

reference_id.description: img_ for images, vid_ for videos, ref_ for type-agnostic ids minted before the media type is known. Readers MUST accept all three; writers SHOULD emit img_/vid_. Minted form: '<img|vid>_' + slugify(source) + '_' + sha256(source+'|'+source_id).slice(0,8).

recipe_id.description: A VisualRecipe. Stable across every content revision.

conflict_id.description: One detected conflict. Deterministic: cfl_ + sha1(category|group|sorted values).slice(0,12).

upload_id.description: Handle for locally held user media. An upl_ handle NEVER implies the bytes left the device.

formatter_mode.description: Prompt formatter target. Reserved: generic (MVP, the only one required), flux, qwen_image, sd, gpt_image, minimax_h3, krea. Open by pattern on purpose: no model backend is ever hardcoded; adding a mode is adding a key.

license_id.description: Normalized license identifier. user_owned = the operator's own local media (never redistributed). Policy classes: allowed by default {public_domain, pdm, cc0, cc_by, user_owned}; optional/opt-in {cc_by_sa}; excluded by default {cc_by_nc, cc_by_nc_sa, cc_by_nd, cc_by_nc_nd, proprietary, unknown}.

license_policy_class.description: Derived from license_id plus operator settings. Advisory cache; recompute on load.

provider_source.description: Provider key. Reserved: wikimedia_commons, openverse, local, user_upload, manual. Open by pattern so providers stay pluggable.

category_arity.description: single_dominant = at most one non-modifier value is physically coherent in one shot; two different dominant values from two different references is a HARD CONFLICT the UI must resolve. multi = values coexist naturally; only shared exclusivity_group or explicit conflicts_with produce a conflict. ARITY IS A CONFLICT-DETECTION RULE, NOT A CARDINALITY CONSTRAINT: no schema sets maxItems on a single_dominant category, because a conflicting state MUST be representable in order to be surfaced.

category_arity_map.$comment: INFORMATIVE CANONICAL CONSTANT (not used for validation). The authoritative arity table.

category_to_prompt_slot_map.$comment: INFORMATIVE CANONICAL CONSTANT (not used for validation). Maps all 20 visual categories onto the 13 StructuredPrompt slots. 'constraints' has no source category: it is fed by chips with negate=true (from ANY category) plus composer-level directives.

prompt_slot_emit_order_map.$comment: INFORMATIVE CANONICAL CONSTANT. Within a slot fed by several categories, fragments are emitted in this category order.

extract_group.description: The eight EXTRACT buttons on a reference card (brief, Explore actions). Each expands to a set of visual categories via extract_group_map.

extract_group_map.$comment: INFORMATIVE CANONICAL CONSTANT. UI EXTRACT group -> visual categories.

taxonomy_file.$comment: Shape of data/taxonomy/<group>.json. A file MAY carry more than one category (the brief ships nine files for twenty categories, e.g. camera.json holds camera_angle + camera_distance + camera_motion).

version.description: Monotonic content revision of this taxonomy file.
